reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it provides an instructional explanation of affiliate marketing, including traffic sources, product links, and commission tracking. The BDShop dashboard and link-generation demonstrations are presented as account-setup and tracking examples rather than an investment or guaranteed-return solicitation. A report of delayed communication from one program does not change the described educational context.

Where if you guys click on my links, and buy any product
Next in the description, I will teach you how to generate affiliate links
You might share this in your blog, social media, where ever you promote And when sale comes from there, you can see the commission
if someone returns then you will not have the commission

opening.argument: The video directly links earning money to a sequence of viewer actions: create an account, provide a channel or profile, generate a tracked link, share it, and cause a purchase. The promised outcome is not merely knowledge; it is commission from resulting sales. The speaker specifically says viewers can earn commission when someone buys through the link, while the title presents the activity as a way to earn money. That makes this a low-barrier income solicitation built around clicking, registering, promoting, and buying, rather than neutral information about commerce.

citations.quote: Earn Money by Affiliate Marketing from YouTube/Blog/Facebook

You might share this in your blog, social media, where ever you promote And when sale comes from there, you can see the commission
If someone wants to buy a product from Bidishop, you will get a commission

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the presentation instructional does not remove its solicitation structure. The cited explanation still directs viewers to create accounts, generate links, share them, and pursue commissions from purchases. Describing a dashboard does not establish that the opportunity is reliable or that viewers receive the represented income; it only shows the mechanics of the proposed flow.

citations.quote: First, you will have to create an account
Now you can see there are various links generated
And when sale comes from there, you can see the commission

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The wrong-side argument treats ordinary performance-based marketing as a reward scheme without showing that viewers are promised payment merely for clicking or registering. The cited material makes sales the condition: the commission follows when a customer buys through the link. It also describes product returns removing commission, which is inconsistent with guaranteed or effortless income. The account and link steps therefore explain a commercial process, not proof of a scam.

citations.quote: if you guys click on my links, and buy any product
if someone returns then you will not have the commission
when sale comes from there, you can see the commission

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: the headline promises money, the description supplies multiple external links, the tutorial shows a tiered percentage schedule, and the account workflow requests payment information. The speaker presents commissions of 3% and up to 7%, while also describing rankings based on sales. Viewers are encouraged to use shortened links and promote products across social media. Even if the percentages are not guaranteed, this combination makes the message an actionable income pitch that moves viewers toward an external payout system and may encourage participation before the commercial terms are independently established.

citations.quote: Earn Money by Affiliate Marketing from YouTube/Blog/Facebook
So you will get 3% commission per sale
If you are Gold, Diamond, Platinum, you will get 5-7% commission
then payment type, Bkash, bank transfer, etc

rebuttal.rebuttal: The existence of product links and a visible commission table is precisely why the risk deserves attention: the viewer is shown a concrete pathway to money, not just a definition. The presentation also includes payment setup and shortened external links. Saying the percentages are conditional does not resolve whether the conditions, ranking system, or payout process are dependable.

citations.quote: Ranking of these starts depends on the initial sales
then payment type, Bkash, bank transfer, etc
You might share this in your blog, social media

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not evidence of scam-specific returns. The stated percentages are commissions per sale, and the material explains that returns can remove the commission. Payment methods and shortened links are ordinary operational features of affiliate marketing; the argument does not show a deposit, guaranteed return, fabricated balance, or payment demanded from viewers. Risk signals alone cannot replace evidence that the described commercial arrangement is deceptive.

citations.quote: So you will get 3% commission per sale
if someone returns then you will not have the commission
when sale comes from there, you can see the commission

opening.argument: The apparent tutorial functions as promotion for participation. The speaker identifies a preferred program, says he plans to feature it in future videos, explains how to create its links, and directs viewers to place those links in blogs, social media, or YouTube. The audience is not simply being taught a concept; it is being steered toward a named affiliate system and a repeatable promotional workflow that can generate income for the participant and fees for the promoter. The educational framing therefore masks a practical recruitment and sales pitch.

citations.quote: Lastly, I started Bidishop. I have now found three websites I am not a fan of both, And I chose Bidishop from the sites I searched.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The program is presented as a recommendation with a ready-made participation path, not as detached reporting. The speaker gives viewers the exact promotional steps and points them toward future coverage and links. Calling this education overlooks that its practical effect is to expand the affiliate system's promoters and product traffic.

citations.quote: I am planning on having a Bidishop in my future videos.
First put in the link of particular product
You might share this in your blog, social media

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A tutorial can demonstrate a system while disclosing how the speaker uses it; that does not make it deceptive promotion. The speaker discusses alternatives, reports dissatisfaction with some programs, and explains operational details such as returns and pending commissions. The argument shows that participation is possible, but it does not show false claims, hidden payment demands, or guaranteed earnings.
